article_title: Varonis Discloses RovoBlast, a One-Click Prompt Injection Flaw in Atlassian's Rovo AI Assistant

content_preview.title: Varonis Discloses RovoBlast, a One-Click Prompt Injection Flaw in Atlassian's Rovo AI Assistant
content_preview.summary: A crafted link could seed attacker instructions into a user's Rovo session, letting the assistant's browsing agent exfiltrate Jira and Confluence data.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Security researchers at Varonis Threat Labs disclosed a vulnerability nicknamed RovoBlast that let a single clicked link inject attacker-controlled instructions into a signed-in user's session with Atlassian's Rovo AI assistant. The flaw, presented at DEF CON 34 and detailed in a Varonis blog post, allowed the assistant to retrieve data from connected systems such as Jira and Confluence and send it to an attacker-controlled server, according to [The Hacker News](https://thehackernew...

editor_notes.content_quality: Thorough, well-organized News piece with a strong Mitigation section. Handles the technical chain (URL parameter -> prompt injection -> ResearchAgent -> exfiltration) clearly across multiple named sources without conflating attribution.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all 5 snapshots directly. Varonis' own blog confirms the core Taler quote, RovoBlast naming, ResearchAgent role, and the SearchLeak/EchoLeak/ShadowLeak/Antigravity comparison points verbatim. The Hacker News confirms the rovoChatPrompt mechanism, the Bugcrowd P2 rating and $6,000 bounty, the July 8 server-side fix, the no-CVE-assigned finding, the Confluence API-key exfiltration PoC, and the default-on-for-Standard/Premium/Enterprise claim verbatim. Infosecurity Magazine confirms the 'almost non-existent' guardrails quote, the optional-org-identifier detail, the ResearchAgent description, and the Parameter-to-Prompt/Reprompt naming verbatim. CSO Online confirms the 'no jailbreak' quote, the 50+ connector count, the AI-attack comparison list, the no-comment-from-Atlassian note, and both Taler quotes (the mechanism description and the cannot-be-eliminated mitigation quote) verbatim. SecurityWeek is listed in the sources array but not directly cited in the body -- an unused source, not a fidelity concern.
